questions.q: What does the WHERE clause do?
options: Filters rows, keeping only those where the condition is true
Sorts the results
Renames a column
Groups rows for aggregation
questions.explain: WHERE is evaluated once per row, and only matching rows appear in the results.

questions.q: Where does WHERE go in a SELECT statement?
options: After FROM
Before SELECT
After ORDER BY
It can go anywhere
questions.explain: The standard order is SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ...

questions.q: How do you write a text value in a WHERE condition?
options: Wrapped in single quotes, e.g. WHERE Color = 'Red'
Wrapped in double quotes only
In square brackets
No quoting is needed for text
questions.explain: Single quotes mark a string literal in T-SQL.

questions.q: Why does 'WHERE DiscountedPrice < 50' fail when DiscountedPrice is a SELECT alias?
options: SQL Server evaluates WHERE before SELECT, so the alias doesn't exist yet at that point
Aliases can never be used anywhere except the SELECT list, ever
It's a typo — DiscountedPrice should be in quotes
WHERE only works with columns that exist in the FROM table's primary key
questions.explain: This is about logical processing order — WHERE runs before the SELECT list (and its aliases) is evaluated.

questions.q: What's the fix for filtering on a value that's only defined as a SELECT alias?
options: Repeat the full expression inside the WHERE clause
There is no fix — this is impossible in T-SQL
Move the WHERE clause after ORDER BY
Use a comment to reference the alias
questions.explain: WHERE ListPrice * 0.9 < 50 works because it re-evaluates the same expression directly, rather than relying on the alias.
